newsitem.title: UK: Precious metals quiet in limited price ranges.
newsitem.headline: Precious metals quiet in limited price ranges.

text.p: Gold prices drifted in a narrow range on Monday afternoon and platinum eased as the precious metals market took a breather from last week's extreme volatility.
"It was a dull morning and it's been a deadly quiet afternoon," a dealer said.
The price of gold fixed at $344.25 an ounce, up just $0.40 from the morning fixing, after its price movements were limited to a range of about $1.00 throughout the day.
Dealers said they were watching Wall Street and the dollar for cues to the gold market's next move.
But gyrations in stock and foreign exchange markets were insufficient for now to attract money to bullion, they added.
The Dow industrials were up around 70 points at the time of the afternoon gold fixing, while the dollar was stabilising above the six-month low against the yen.
Platinum, meanwhile, continued to drift down from last week's highs of around $500 an ounce as jittery trading tailed off.
It was last indicated at $464.00/$469.00 after sliding lower shortly after New York opened, from $475.00/$505.00 at Friday's finish and London's afternoon fixing of $475.00.
Prices for platinum and palladium have soared this year, and especially in recent weeks, due to tightness in the market resulting from delayed exports from key producer Russia.
Palladium was slightly firmer at $223.00/$233.00, up some $4.00 from Friday's close and near the latest 17-year highs hit last week.
Both metals were vulnerable to further spikes in the near term, particularly if spreads flared back out to $30 as they had last week, dealers said.
"You only have to do a couple of deals like that and the price moves out $50-$60," one said.
Silver six cents easier at $4.82/$4.84 and like gold was uneventfully holding to a narrow range.
Silver has been attracting speculative interest which has caused moves in the one-three months contango recently.
One dealer said the halving of the nearby contango to two percent from four percent indicated a large short position had been established in the market.
